newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SGB still interested in Generale Bank, BBL merger.
newsitem.headline: SGB still interested in Generale Bank, BBL merger.

text.p: Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique SA (SGB) said on Thursday it was still interested in a possible merger between its unit Generale Bank and Banque Bruxelles Lambert (BBL).
But SGB chairman Etienne Davignon, in a interview with Reuters, said that the project was still blocked by Internationale Nederlanden Groep (ING). Dutch ING is one of BBL's leading shareholders.
"At this moment, the project is in the freezer," he said.
"If anything would change, a merger between BBL and Generale Bank would still be a good business proposal and a project we would be happy to look at," he said.
"But other shareholders have a different view on this," he said. Asked whether he meant ING, he said "yes".
"There is no movement on that front," he said.
The stock prices of BBL and Generale Bank flared at the start of last year, after Davignon said he backed the idea of creating one big Belgian bank.
But the merger project was abandonned in April 1996. Davignon said last year that ING stood in the way of a merger.
ING has said it will defend its BBL stake but has never made clear if, under certain conditions, it would be willing to allow a merger. ING controls 20 percent of BBL stock.
